scope: Proposition 19.5 (Global static classification) of the manuscript “Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Equality-and-rigidity-in-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f1aab59ba484eb8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 147-148. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The positive component is the whole original open exterior: U = int Ω and N > 0 there. Its attached boundary is S. There is a global isometry of the static base onto the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spatial exterior of mass m, under which hb = (︃ 1 + m 2ρ2 )︃2 ( dρ2 + ρ2 gS3 ), λ = 1 − m/(2ρ2) 1 + m/(2ρ2) , ρ ≥ √︂ m/2. (19.26) The isometry is smooth on the open base and in its one-sided regular boundary structure. The attachment is homeomorphic to the original attachment of S in Ω and restricts smoothly on 147 S. In particular the open base is simply connected and S is a round three-sphere in its induced metric. The base reflection is smooth in signed λ in the positive boundary-lapse case; its angular coordinates can be taken constant along base normal geodesics.
